messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.content:
**Answer**

The total entropy change for heating a 1 kg ice block from 0 °C to 100 °C at 1 atm consists of three reversible processes:

| Process | ΔS (J K⁻¹) |
|---------|-----------|
| Melting (ice → water at 0 °C) | \( \displaystyle \Delta S_{\text{melt}} = \frac{m\,L_f}{T} = \frac{1\;\text{kg}\times 334\,000\;\text{J kg}^{-1}}{273.15\;\text{K}} \approx 1\,222\;\text{J K}^{-1} \) |
| Heating liquid water (0 °C → 100 °C) | \( \displaystyle \Delta S_{\text{heat,liq}} = m\,c_{\text{water}}\ln\!\left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right) = 1\;\text{kg}\times 4\,184\;\text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\times \ln\!\left(\frac{373.15}{273.15}\right) \approx 1\,307\;\text{J K}^{-1} \) |
| Boiling (water → steam at 100 °C) | \( \displaystyle \Delta S_{\text{boil}} = \frac{m\,L_v}{T} = \frac{1\;\text{kg}\times 2\,257\,000\;\text{J kg}^{-1}}{373.15\;\text{K}} \approx 6\,050\;\text{J K}^{-1} \) |

Adding them up:

\[
\boxed{\Delta S_{\text{total}} \approx 1\,222 + 1\,307 + 6\,050 \;\text{J K}^{-1} \approx 8\,579\;\text{J K}^{-1}}
\]

So the 1‑kg ice block gains roughly **8.6 kJ K⁻¹** of entropy when heated from 0 °C to 100 °C at 1 atm.

2. Heating liquid water from 0°C to 100°C: use specific heat capacity c_water = 4184 J/(kg·K). ΔT = 100°C - 0°C = 100 K.
